gloss: to look forward to; to eagerly await

definitions.gloss: to look forward to; to eagerly await
definitions.explanation: to anticipate something with pleasure and excitement

examples.japanese: ⟦{週末|しゅうまつ}→週末：03030_shuumatsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{楽|たの}しみにして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: I'm looking forward to the weekend.

examples.japanese: お⟦{会|あ}い→会う：00482_au⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{楽|たの}しみにして⟦います→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: I look forward to meeting you.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧たち⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{遠足|えんそく}→遠足：04107_ensoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{楽|たの}しみにして⟦いて→いる：00495_iru⟧、⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{晩|ばん}→晩：00542_ban⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{眠|ねむ}れなかった→眠れる：15166_nemureru⟧らしい。
examples.english: The children were so looking forward to the field trip that they apparently couldn't sleep the night before.

notes:
One of the most common expressions for anticipation in Japanese. Almost always appears in the て⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ form ({楽|たの}しみにして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧) to express an ongoing state of looking forward to something. The polite form {楽|たの}しみにして⟦います→いる：00495_iru⟧ is a standard closing phrase in business emails and conversations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {楽|たの}しみにして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧: am looking forward to
- {楽|たの}しみにして⟦います→いる：00495_iru⟧: look forward to (polite)
- {楽|たの}しみにして⟦おります→おる：01324_oru⟧: look forward to (humble/formal)
- {楽|たの}しみにして⟦いて→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧: look forward to it! (casual)
- ⟦{楽|たの}しみ→楽しみ：01651_tanoshimi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お⟦{待|ま}ち→待つ：00469_matsu⟧⟦しています→する：00392_suru⟧: looking forward to it (polite business)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{待|ま}ち{遠|どお}しい→待ち遠しい：14726_machidooshii⟧: can hardly wait — emphasizes impatience and the feeling that time is passing too slowly
- ⟦わくわくする→ワクワクする：25801_wakuwakusuru⟧: to be excited — focuses on the excited feeling itself rather than anticipation
- ⟦{心待|こころま}ち→心待ち：12605_kokoromachi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to eagerly await — more literary and formal

USAGE:
In email sign-offs, {楽|たの}しみにして⟦います→いる：00495_iru⟧ is equivalent to English "I look forward to..." and is appropriate in both business and casual correspondence.
